display_name: Mailama, Master of the Monsoon Tanks
one_line: Kakatiya-era hydraulic engineer overseeing Dharmakirti-samudra and plateau tanks across Telangana.

appearance.age_look: late 30s, lean but strong, medium height with a craftsman’s build
appearance.face: oval face, warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard, sharp observant eyes, default expression a focused, calm half-smile as if gauging water levels.
appearance.hair: thick black hair, medium length and combed back; covered by a deep-maroon cotton turban (paga) wrapped low and secure, with a simple gold-toned cloth band at the front and no plume.
appearance.costume: knee-length off-white handwoven cotton angarakha-style tunic crossing right over left and tied with side cords; over it a sleeveless, hip-length dark-indigo cotton waistcoat with subtle narrow block-printed stripes; lower body in a mustard-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped in Kakatiya-style with neat front pleats, reaching the ankles; simple leather sandals; a thin dark-brown cotton patika sash diagonally from right shoulder to left hip, used to hold measuring cords; accessories include a narrow copper armlet on his right arm, a simple black-bead and copper pendant necklace, and a palm-leaf roll tucked at his back waist to suggest plans and inscriptions.
appearance.signature: a long wooden measuring staff, shoulder-height, with carved depth marks and a simple bronze-tipped end, held in his right hand and often rested lightly on the ground near an imagined tank embankment.

ref_desc: Mailama is a lean, medium-brown Kakatiya engineer with a maroon turban, short beard, off-white angarakha, indigo waistcoat, mustard dhoti, diagonal sash and copper ornaments, carrying a marked wooden measuring staff in a palette of off-white, indigo and ochre.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Mailama, a Kakatiya-period hydraulic engineer: a lean, medium-brown man in his late thirties with an oval face, sharp eyes, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard, wearing a deep-maroon cotton turban wrapped low, off-white angarakha tunic crossing right over left, dark-indigo sleeveless waistcoat with subtle stripes, and a mustard-ochre cotton dhoti pleated and reaching his ankles, plus simple leather sandals. Add a thin dark-brown sash running diagonally from right shoulder to left hip, a narrow copper armlet, a black-bead necklace with a small copper pendant, and a rolled palm-leaf tucked at his back waist. His signature wooden measuring staff, shoulder-height with carved depth marks and a bronze-tipped end, should be clearly visible in his hand. Use off-white, dark indigo, mustard ochre, deep maroon and warm brown as dominant colours, and present him from front, three-quarter, and side views to emphasize consistent hair, face, clothing folds and staff details.
